value.rationale: The convex Euclidean approximation gap between the full binary cube and the standard first-order Reed-Muller codeword polytope is a natural exact geometric invariant for an infinite family, with explicit nearest-face classification for every received vector. Bent vertices are identified as precisely all farthest points, and all project into simplex facets. This distinguishes convex nearest-point geometry from known discrete Hamming covering radius and supplies a reproducible exact projection algorithm. The result is not merely a finite codeword distance table.
